answers.explanation: Carry the physical, current AF Form 483 while operating. A photograph of the license is not a substitute. This practice app does not issue the card.
The local supplement requires CBT and testing through ADTCS, with alternate documentation for personnel unable to access it.
Complete annual refresher training through ADTCS and review the instruction. Your Unit ADPM tracks completion.
Aircraft in motion have the first right-of-way priority. Emergency vehicles do not automatically assume right of way.
Routine vehicle operations use the right-hand side to improve visibility of signage; the supplement identifies duty-related exceptions.
Keep at least 50 feet clear unless specifically authorized by applicable regulations or guidance.
The general-purpose taxiway limit is 15 mph. An approved local supplement can specify an exception.
The local parallel-taxiway limit is 25 mph. Conditions may require a lower speed; this is not permission to enter a CMA.
Slow to 5 mph within 50 feet of aircraft. Separate aircraft clearance restrictions still apply.
Reduce speed to a maximum of 10 mph, defer vehicle operation when possible, and limit it to mission-essential operations.
The aircraft towing speed limit is 5 mph.
Special-purpose vehicles have a 10 mph taxiway limit.
Keep at least 25 feet in front and 200 feet behind. Units may require additional aircraft-specific safety distances.
Do not operate vehicles within 100 feet of a helicopter with moving rotors.
Position the driver’s side toward the aircraft without interfering with towing or taxiing.
A spotter and prepositioned wheel chocks help prevent a backing vehicle from contacting the aircraft.
Inspect the full tire surface by moving forward as needed, secure loose components and cargo, and check for damaged or loose parts.
Perform a FOD check at every marked or signed checkpoint. Also check tires when returning to pavement from unimproved surfaces.

Cellphone usage is prohibited within the CMA. The local paragraph also requires vehicles to be stopped and positioned so they do not impede aircraft when using a phone. For radio failure, vacate the runway and follow the lost-communication procedure.
Elmendorf’s local instruction requires a stop and permission at the instrument hold position when present, not only in poor weather.
Winter operations can fade markings. Use the hold signs and runway guard lights as additional visual cues.
The supplement accounts for seasonal daylight. The Unit ADPM documents the waiver; required night orientation must be completed no later than 1 October.
Entry is authorized only through designated ECPs. Airfield driving certification does not replace restricted-area access authorization.
Read back the complete instruction, including route and hold-short restrictions.
“Go ahead” is an invitation to speak. It does not grant movement clearance.
Clarify an unclear instruction before taking any action. Do not infer a clearance.
“Roger” acknowledges receipt. It does not replace required readbacks or grant movement clearance.
“Negative” is a denial or correction; resolve the instruction with ATC rather than treating it as approval.
Read back the hold-short instruction and runway designation. Airfield 1 is listed as a 3 OSS call sign; this is a simulated instruction.
Tell ATC when the crossing is complete and identify the exit location. Use your approved call sign.
Use the aviation phonetic alphabet to reduce confusion between letters.
Approved call signs prevent confusion. Elmendorf call signs are listed in Attachment 11.
Daily CMA vehicles need a mounted radio for ATC communication. Test the radio before entering the airfield.
Keep monitoring the appropriate frequency throughout CMA operations.
A steady red signal means stop. Know all tower light-gun signals before driving on the airfield.
Flashing white directs a vehicle to return to its starting point.
Alternating red and green is a general warning, requiring extreme caution.
Do not enter the CMA without specific tower approval. Qualified escorts must meet the applicable clearance requirements.
Request permission about 100 feet before the hold line to allow time to resolve miscommunications. Stop short unless cleared.
Flashing runway edge lights indicate a problem or emergency requiring immediate runway exit.
Vacate the runway immediately and report being off, along with relevant safety information. Use a phone if radio communication is unavailable.
Headlight signaling is a fallback after vacating the runway when other communication is not practical.
A standing or blanket approval does not authorize runway entry.
Use the specified conspicuity lighting while driving in the CMA.
Permission inside an instrument critical area can be requested independently of permission onto the runway.
Only a CMA-qualified escort may provide escort into the CMA.
The escort must keep the group visible and nearby, and relay ATC instructions.
Do not use aircraft movement areas for convenience. Plan a route that minimizes required access and crossings.
Use every means to alert nearby taxiing aircraft. State the emergency and location; seek assistance to remove the vehicle safely.
The diagram identifies the east–west runway as 06/24. Study both ends and the nearby hold positions.
The north–south runway is labeled 16/34 in Attachment 13.
The legend uses light blue for the CMA. Operational boundaries must be learned using the current WADPM-issued diagram.
Instrument hold lines are represented in red in this diagram’s legend. Pavement markings themselves are yellow.
The diagram legend uses yellow for VFR hold lines. Stop short and obtain the required ATC clearance.
Red shading denotes restricted areas. Observe local access authorization and ECP procedures.
Locate the Airfield Management and Tower labels south of runway 06/24. Use the full-size diagram to study the surrounding routes.
The solid lines face the approach side and the dashed lines face the runway. Stop short and obtain clearance before crossing.
